{
  "verdict": "revise",
  "score": 0.45,
  "reasons": [
    "Correctness checks will attempt naive_recursive(50), (100), (500) which are infeasible to complete in reasonable time, causing the test run to hang or time out.",
    "test_fib.py currently marks naive_recursive timings as skipped only in code path; the correctness checks still call naive for all sample inputs, which contradicts feasibility.",
    "stdout/stderr capture fields in fib_results.json are not truly capturing the runtime stdout/stderr streams; artifact stores summary in 'stdout' but does not capture raw stdout/stderr separately.",
    "No fib_cache.py code excerpt is shown; ensure the artifact includes a working fib_cache.py with naive_recursive, cached_recursive using lru_cache, and iterative; the test script assumes these exist and behave as described.",
    "Potential risk: if fib_cache.naive_recursive is extremely slow at moderate n, the correctness tests will take too long; need guard or smaller test set or separate test modes."
  ],
  "guidance": "Modify test_fib.py to avoid correctness checks for naive_recursive on large n (e.g., limit naive checks to n <= 20 or 25). Compute oracle results for all sample inputs using iterative, but only compare naive and cached for small n. Alternatively, split checks into correctness (small n) and benchmarking (timings) with separate sizes. Ensure timings include a real run for all three functions where feasible. Update the artifact to capture true stdout/stderr (redirect and store). Ensure fib_results.json includes actual source contents for fib_cache.py and test_fib.py."
}
